answer: Payouts climb a terrace: each higher tier pays more but demands fresh proof of live work, carried by a raven — a stranger courier drawn at random who delivers the claim to an unrelated verifier, paid only if the proof checks out. Every claim leaves a plume, a public trail linking its proofs, so auditors spot clones whose plumes converge on one operator. Tiers narrow as they rise, so n clones cannot all sit high; each clone pays its own fee and bond, yet a crowded tier splits one payout among occupants — per-clone revenue falls as 1/n while cost grows with n.
